• CBI is NOT a constitutional body.
• Works under DSPE Act, 1946.
• Requires state consent.
• Director has a minimum tenure of 2 years.
• CVC supervises CBI in corruption cases.
CBI is NOT a constitutional body.

items: Exams frequently trick candidates by labeling CBI as a constitutional or statutory body created by a standalone Act—it derives powers solely from the DSPE Act, 1946.
Note that state consent is a mandatory requirement for CBI investigations inside state territory.
Supervision of CBI is divided: CVC supervises it specifically for corruption cases, not all criminal investigations.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: CBI is not a constitutional body and functions under the DSPE Act, 1946.
The agency requires state consent before undertaking investigations within a state's jurisdiction.
The Director of CBI is legally guaranteed a minimum tenure of 2 years.
Superintendence over CBI regarding corruption offences lies with the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC).
